headline: The fully matched game becomes easier for contributors to navigate
summary: Contributors get readable names, shared structures, folders organised by system and tools that reject changes which break matching. The snapshot still reports all 5,116 functions and all code bytes matched: matching means compiling to the original game's exact bytes. This is source cleanup rather than new player features, and the changes repeatedly report unchanged loaded bytes across versions.
highlights: The day's 231,369 additions and 208,167 deletions mostly reflect formatting: #169 alone adds 169,328 lines and removes 147,550, without changing loaded bytes.
Game data and pointer blocks now build from C, with values generated from contributors' own discs rather than committed retail values (#196, #197, #198).
Named buttons, levels, hero states and object classes replace opaque numbers; core files and game folders gain readable organisation (#186, #188, #189, #190, #191, #192).

Unnecessary matching tricks were removed, while required exceptions retain explanations. Some private views remain because converting them changes bytes; syntax errors remain documented (#174, #195, #202).
Contributor documentation now explains locations, checks and remaining work; local matching checks still require the disc and toolchain (#168, #210).
